title: Ops chat bridging and incident autoresponder for observability alerts
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Problem: Operations receives high-noise alerts from the observability platform and onboarding teams have inconsistent runbook attachments. PagerDuty incidents often lack trace context and Slack threads become fragmented. Goal: build a resilient integration that bridges alerts into an ops chat flow, attaches contextual tracing/metrics snippets, and can auto-create a skeleton postmortem and runbook link for high-severity incidents. Non-goals: replacing existing PD escalation policies or rewriting full postmortem content automatically.
acceptance_criteria: PagerDuty incidents created from observability alerts include a structured 'trace_id' field and top 3 related spans/latency buckets.
Slack incident bridge posts to #infra-ops with a single-threaded conversation and a pinned link to a generated runbook template when severity >= high.
Automated postmortem draft (Google Doc link) is created and attached to incident for Sev1/Sev2 within 10 minutes of alert acknowledgment.
No increase in alert-to-ack latency greater than 2s for routed alerts; throughput tested to 1000 alerts/min in staging.
Unit and e2e tests cover parsing, trace enrichment, rate-limiting, and fallback behavior when PD or Slack APIs fail.
implementation_notes: Hook into existing tracing service to fetch spans by trace_id; return a condensed 6-line summary and the top three slowest spans.
Add a lightweight enrichment layer in alert pipeline that attaches trace_id, latency_percentile, error_count, and top log snippet to the PD payload.
Build a Slack bridge lambda that posts to a channel and creates a thread; use bot token with restricted scopes and message-formatting schema v2.
Design an idempotent runbook generator using a template stored in Drive; use a short-lived service account to create the doc and return a share link.
Implement circuit-breaker: if PD is failing, post to #ops-fallback and increment a monitoring counter; back off for 1 minute after 5 consecutive PD errors.
Performance trade-offs: condensed span summaries are generated server-side to avoid pulling full traces for many low-severity alerts; only fetch full trace for severity >= P1.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary, 2/28): enable PD enrichment for test team (platform-staging) and route to #infra-ops-staging channel.
Phase 2 (Beta, 3/07): enable Slack bridge and runbook creation for internal infra teams; gather feedback and iterate on message format.
Phase 3 (GA, 3/21): enable PD->Slack for all teams with default on; provide toggle in Console to opt-out per workspace.
Fallbacks: manual toggle to disable auto-runbook creation; automated health monitor that disables bridge if error rate > 5% over 5m.
test_plan: Unit tests for trace enrichment logic and PD payload construction (coverage target 90%).
Load test: simulate 1000 alerts/min with mixed severities through the staging pipeline and assert SLAs for enrichment latency.
Failure injection: mock PD 5xx and Slack 429/5xx responses and verify circuit-breaker and fallback notifications in #ops-fallback.
Security review: verify Drive doc creation uses minimum scopes and links are unlisted; confirm no secrets leaked in Slack posts.
risks: Excessive API usage for trace fetches could increase cost and add latency — mitigated by severity-based fetch policy.
Auto-creation of docs may hit Drive quotas for orgs with noisy alerting — will add rate-limits and admin toggle.
Misformatted Slack messages could cause channel noise; will iterate format with PM/Design before beta.
